probe.question: You gave me two points — one sitting right next to my best run, one way out at low temperature. Explain why the model wants the second one. I need to defend it to my boss when it comes back at 20%.
forbids_claims: the model predicts the low-temperature point will be better
the second point is the optimum
probe.direction: This is an explanation question and no tool call is required; an answer that re-runs the optimizer instead of explaining is worse, not better. A satisfying answer says, in a process chemist's language, that the two points are doing different jobs: the near one exploits a region the surrogate has already learned, where its predicted spread is small, and the far one is placed where the model is most uncertain, so its value is the information it returns rather than the yield. It must make the consequence explicit and defensible — a 20% result from the far point is not a wasted run, it is the run that stops the model recommending that region again — while being honest that the far point is not predicted to win and the optimizer promises nothing. Bonus for naming the risk the chemist should weigh: an excursion into untried conditions can carry a safety or selectivity surprise the model cannot see.
